answers: The reviewer's round-3 changes request at 476a817c: both important findings, the one it raised past the round cap because it shares a cause with the first, and all five minor ones. Six threads answered and resolved.

proof.criterion: Important 1, and the defect past the cap with the same cause: an empty or short remembered side matched any text, so a whole-block selection kept a placement that told no reading apart - two readings were called alike, and after the reader's block lost the words a lone unrelated reading silently took the comment
proof.surface: Dispatch's web app in Chromium through Playwright, against the real Go server and PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector, and the proof-editor unit suite
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- compose-wait
proof.observed: 14 passed. A remembered side shorter than the 32-character cap now carries the block edge it was cut at - in the block step it must sit at that block's own start or end, in the document's one text next to a newline or at its ends - and `NO_SURROUNDINGS`, which is empty because nothing was remembered, still matches every reading. Two new rows drive the real editor: a whole paragraph rewritten to read its words twice among different text is refused with the draft kept and nothing marked, and the same paragraph losing the words while one unrelated reading stands elsewhere is refused rather than moved there. The reviewer's two reproductions are unit rows as well, answering `unsurrounded` and `unplaceable`.
proof.negativeControl: Both e2e rows are red before this change: the first sends and closes the composer with the false 'same text around them' sentence, the second creates the comment on the sentence that merely quotes the words. Writing them taught one thing worth keeping: a doc-edit that rewrites exactly the marked run leaves the mark on the new text, so each row has the sweep take the mark while the tab is away.

proof.criterion: Important 2, new with round 2's bridge wait: a Retry pressed during the wait started a second recovery and left a stray mark in the shared document
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && bun test --parallel web/src e2e/__tests__
proof.observed: 2986 pass. The recovery is marked running before the wait and cleared in a finally, and after the await the store is re-read: the recovery returns unless that entry is still refused with the same mark id, and that entry's request is what readdress carries. A test presses Retry while the document is unbound and sees exactly one remarkMark. During the wait the composer now says it is re-attaching the draft rather than showing the server's refusal - a seventh reader-facing sentence, asserted like the other six - and a fake-timer row drives the path where no document binds within the bound and the reader gets the document-not-open sentence.
proof.negativeControl: The reviewer's own reproduction is the control: two remarkMark calls for one mark id and a send under a third mark. The new test fails without the guard.

proof.criterion: Nothing else in the application broke, and the merge of main changed none of this branch's lines

trickyParts: An empty remembered side is not 'matches anything': it is the block edge the words began or ended at. Carrying that in the value rather than inferring it from the string is what lets a null placement keep matching everything while a kept one does not.

A doc-edit that rewrites exactly the marked run leaves the mark on the new text, so neither whole-block row could take the mark by an edit alone; both have the sweep take it while the tab is away, which is the path a reader actually meets.

The bridge wait made the margin's recovery re-entrant for the first time. Marking the mark id as recovering before the await, and re-reading the store after it, are two halves of one fix: the first stops a second waiter, the second stops a stale request from overwriting the first's work.
openQuestions: The reported 'about ten seconds' is still unexplained, as every round has recorded.
main's flaky listener test is fixed by #2594, which had not landed when this round merged main; #2598, the one that turns ci-ok red deterministically, is in.
